Successfully installed ... openvino-genai-2026.4.0.0 openvino-tokenizers-2026.4.0.0 ... (installed transitively via the whowhatbench/optimum-intel dependency chain, pulled from PyPI rather than the job's locally-built OpenVINO wheel)
root_cause: The job_llm_accuracy_tests.yml workflow explicitly installs the locally-built 'openvino' and 'openvino_tokenizers' wheels via the install_ov_wheels composite action, but the subsequent 'pip install -r tests/llm/requirements.txt' step pulls in 'whowhatbench' (from openvino.genai git subdirectory) which depends on 'optimum-intel[nncf,tests]', which transitively requires 'openvino-genai'. Pip resolves and installs 'openvino-genai-2026.4.0.0' and 'openvino-tokenizers-2026.4.0.0' from the public/proxy index as prebuilt wheels bundling their own libopenvino.so with SOVERSION 2640 embedded rpath, while overwriting/shadowing the previously-installed local 'openvino_tokenizers' wheel (log shows 'Uninstalling openvino-tokenizers-2026.4.1.0' then reinstalling 2026.4.0.0). The 'openvino_genai' native extension (py_openvino_genai) then looks for its bundled libopenvino.so.2640 which pip's dependency resolver did not actually provision (only the metadata/wheel for openvino-genai's Python side was pulled, not the matching core runtime it was linked against), causing the shared-library load to fail at import time. This affected both CPU and iGPU device variants identically, since the requirements install step is device-agnostic and runs before the device-specific pytest invocation.
reproduction_steps: In a fresh venv: 1) pip install <local openvino wheel> <local openvino_tokenizers wheel>; 2) pip install -r tests/llm/requirements.txt (which pulls whowhatbench from openvino.genai git + optimum-intel[nncf,tests]); 3) python3 -c "import openvino_genai" -> reproduces ImportError: libopenvino.so.2640: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory.
recommended_actions: Pin 'openvino-genai' (and its embedded openvino/openvino-tokenizers versions) as a locally-built wheel dependency in tests/llm/requirements.txt or install it explicitly via install_ov_wheels alongside 'openvino' and 'openvino_tokenizers', instead of letting pip resolve it transitively from the index.

Add a '--no-deps' or constraint entry in tests/constraints.txt to prevent pip from silently reinstalling a different-versioned openvino-tokenizers/openvino-genai during the 'pip install -r requirements.txt' step.

After installing test requirements, run 'python3 -c "import openvino_genai"' as a fast-fail sanity check step before running the full pytest suite, to catch this class of ABI/version mismatch earlier with a clearer error.
Verify LD_LIBRARY_PATH / RPATH setup is not being overridden when the transitively-installed openvino-genai wheel takes precedence over the locally built one.
prevention_strategies: Add an explicit version constraint (or the locally-built wheel path) for openvino-genai and openvino-tokenizers in tests/llm/constraints.txt so pip cannot silently swap in a different, un-linked prebuilt runtime during transitive dependency resolution. Consider a CI smoke-import step immediately after wheel installation for any job that installs additional OpenVINO-dependent python packages.
historical_context: No prior investigation with this exact signature (libopenvino.so.2640 ImportError) was found in the CI Doctor MQ pattern database; this appears to be a new failure mode, first observed in this run for both the CPU and iGPU LLM accuracy jobs simultaneously.
